summary: Louisiana Division of Forestry steel lookout described by NGS in 1971 at 110 ft overall; Forest Lookouts marks it removed with no date. Town is in Vernon Parish; tower listed in Sabine.

facts.design: Four-legged steel structure, painted silver, with a cabin on top (1971 survey description)
facts.agency: Louisiana Division of Forestry (per the 1971 survey description)
facts.status_note: Listed as removed, with no date; the survey file has no entry after 1971

events.note: National Geodetic Survey described the tower; the survey file's only history entry

evidence.supports: four-legged steel structure, painted silver, with a cabin
evidence.quote: IT IS A FOUR-LEGGED STEEL STRUCTURE, PAINTED SILVER, WITH A CABIN

evidence.supports: cabin on top; overall height 110 feet
evidence.quote: ON TOP AND THE OVERALL HEIGHT IS 110 FEET

evidence.supports: owner is the Louisiana Division of Forestry
evidence.quote: HORNBECK LOOKOUT TOWER BELONGS TO THE LOUISIANA DIVISION OF
IT IS LOCATED 2-1/2 MILES SOUTHWEST OF HORNBECK

evidence.supports: town of Hornbeck lies in Vernon Parish
evidence.quote: Location of Hornbeck in Vernon Parish, Louisiana.

corrections.why: The agency field holds the township, range and section from the Forest Lookouts page, a land location. The 1971 NGS description names the Louisiana Division of Forestry as owner (the survey spells it 'Forestery').

notes_for_editor: Parish conflict, not corrected: the Forest Lookouts page and the NGS datasheet (STATE/COUNTY LA/SABINE) put the tower in Sabine Parish, while Wikipedia places the town of Hornbeck in Vernon Parish. Both can be true, since the tower is 2.5 miles from the town, but no source says so; the story reports the disagreement. The NGS 110 ft is the overall height including the cabin, so it is not entered as height_m, which the guide defines as height to the cab floor. No built date, staffing or fire history found in two web searches or the pages read.
